scope: Complete modern four-weight flywheel demonstration selected from the balanced-rotation questions on Madrid I114r. The rigid four-spoke arrangement is an explicit assumption, not a tracing of one labelled variant.

date.note: Approximate manuscript dating, not a dated completion record.

folio.verification_note: Edition foliation and text verified through e-Leo. Original-holder service may be unavailable. e-Leo viewer is an authorised-edition resource, not the original holding institution.

scale_m.note: Full swept bound. All chosen dimensions are modern explanatory assumptions, never claimed measurements of a historical machine.

frame.transforms: All part positions relative to their named parent. Joint q is an extra rotation or translation about the declared parent-frame pivot applied to the rest transform. Children inherit it once.

assumptions.statement: Every numerical part size, position, orientation and support arrangement in parts is a declared modern modelling choice unless a separate primary source is explicitly attached. Materials marked assumed are plausible period choices. They are not measured from any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: Leonardo did not provide a manufacturing drawing with all dimensions.

assumptions.statement: The stated rates and loads are slow modern demonstration choices. They do not reproduce a measured speed in Leonardo s workshop.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating record was located.

assumptions.statement: The fixed support is bored to radius 0.045 m around the radius 0.04 m rotor shaft. Its lower thrust pad ends at y=0.60 m, tangent to the shaft end. Bearing friction is not quantified.
assumptions.reason: Complete the numerical modern demonstration without presenting invented details as Leonardo dimensions.

dimensions_m.closure: Close last point to first. Revolve closed section through 2*pi. Ends are annular, bore remains open.

input_rate.note: Visible external hand input maintains5rpm at q. The drive supplies drag losses. No self-driving motion is claimed.

drive.justification: Visible external hand input maintains5rpm at q. The drive supplies drag losses. No self-driving motion is claimed.

motion.visitor_12s: One slow turn. Angle accumulates. Continuous human input is named on the label.

animation_notes: No bounce, no hidden energy recharge and no invisible reset.
All independent joints are in the schedule. Rigid descendants follow their parent.
Use the specified SI time without cinematic speed-up.

research.sheet_vs_reconstruction: Six motion arrangements and the relation between driving and driven bodies are discussed [EL-FLY]. Mario Taddei lists a flywheel reconstruction [FLY-M]. This four-weight stand is independent modern explanatory geometry.
research.dimensions: No explicit physical dimensions or Richter number verified [EL-FLY]. No braccio conversion made.

claims.claimed_by_leonardo: Leonardo compares balanced and unbalanced rotating weights and rejects the driven body as its own source [EL-FLY].
claims.tested_by_leonardo: No dated experiment by Leonardo was verified in the sources listed here. This is an evidence gap, not proof that he never tried it.
claims.built_in_lifetime: No lifetime build verified. Modern reconstructor inventory does not prove one [FLY-M].
claims.later_tests: No measured modern test found for this exact study.

physics.limits: Lower-bound point-mass calculation excludes finite ball radii, shaft and spokes. No claim of original mass or power gain.
physics.verdict_en: A flywheel stores supplied work and gives it back with losses.
physics.verdict_de: Ein Schwungrad speichert zugeführte Arbeit und gibt sie mit Verlusten wieder ab.

myths.correction: Stored rotational energy comes from its driver. The source itself distinguishes cause and driven motion [EL-FLY].

research.confidence: High transcription. Low exact original geometry. Modern demonstration complete within stated scope.
